name: Fotheringhay Bridge

layers.essential_history: [[c:People once crossed the Nene here by a ford next to the castle. Elizabeth I ordered the first bridge in 1573, and the present stone bridge was built in 1722 by George Portwood of Stamford.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:Take care: there is traffic on the bridge. The view of the church from here is one of the best in the county.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:The ferryman kept a tally of who crossed the ford that night.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The ferry tally]]
material: [[c:Nine o'clock: Will Hobbs, home to the far bank.]]
[[c:Ten o'clock: Master Venn, over, with a sack.]]
[[c:Eleven o'clock: Master Venn, back, no sack.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Who crossed twice? (surname)]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:Master Venn crossed twice: over with a sack, back with nothing.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? Take a hint: hints are free.]]

evidence: [[c:Master Venn crossed the ford twice: over with a sack, back without it.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:Head east, about 160 metres as the crow flies, to the castle mound. Follow the path to the castle mound by the river. Keep to pavements and public paths.]]
